Mode: smear: previous output is advected along the flow and mixed with the source. warp: source is displaced by the flow. viz: flow shown as colour (hue = direction, brightness = speed).
Gain: Strength of the effect, or brightness of the flow visualisation.
Persistence: Smear mode: how much of the previous frame is kept. Near 1 = long trails.
Smoothing: Temporal smoothing of the flow. 0 = raw.
Iterations: Lucas-Kanade refinement passes (1-3). More = better for larger motion, slower.
Regularization: Damps noisy vectors in flat areas. Higher = fewer false vectors but weaker flow.
Active: On: compute flow and update feedback. Off: freeze.
Flowscale: Scale of the flow computation relative to the output. Larger for subtle motion, smaller for fast motion.
Look: original: the internal demo source keeps its colours. mono: demo source becomes black, bone-white and grey. Only affects the demo shown with in1 unconnected.
Accent: Amount (0-1) of red accent tinted onto one object of the demo source (in1 unconnected). Has no effect on a connected in1.
Mix: Blend between the input (0) and the effect (1).
Bypass: Pass in1 through unchanged; the effect does not cook.
Resolutionmode: input: follow in1's resolution (or the demo source when unconnected). custom: use Resolution.
Resolution: Output size in pixels when Resolutionmode is custom.
